front: What is a water molecule made of?
back: Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom (H₂O).
A liquid in which other substances dissolve. Water is the solvent in living organisms.
Enzymes act on food in solution; the small soluble products dissolve so they can be absorbed.
Plasma carries dissolved glucose, amino acids, urea, hormones and CO₂; xylem carries dissolved ions; phloem carries dissolved sucrose.
Urea and excess salts are removed dissolved in water, as urine.

front: Why does the transparency of water matter?
back: Light passes through it, so water plants and algae can photosynthesise below the surface.

front: Why does water's high specific heat capacity matter?
back: Water warms and cools slowly, so lakes, rivers and organisms keep a steady temperature.

front: How does water help to cool organisms?
back: Evaporating water (sweat, transpiration) takes heat energy from the body or leaf.

front: Roughly how much of an adult human's body mass is water?
notes: More than 90% of a lettuce leaf is water.
